full_judgment:
7. It appears that before the High Court Division another question, namely, the defect as to non-joiner of parties was argued on behalf of the defendants appellants, and the High Court Division accepted their contention, as has been noticed above, although they said deflect was not pleaded in the suit nor any issue was framed on the said question. The only issue as to defect o f parties which was framed was as to mis-joinder of parties for imp leading plaintiff's No. 2 to 5 as plaintiffs along with plaintiff's No. 1, which was decided in favour of the plaintiffs. Although no special leave was granted on the question of defect of parties in the appeal before us the point as to non-joiner of certain persons who appear to have acquired some interest in the disputed properties on the basis of several deeds of transfer, Ext. 10 series, executed by some of the plaintiffs in respect of some lands appertaining to the disputed properties, was sought to be argued on behalf of the defendants respondents. The learned Judges of the High Court Division took the view on the basis of the said deeds that the transferees of the said deeds were necessary parties in the suit and that the suit was not maintainable in the absence of such parties. The question of non-joiner of the said parties having been raised on behalf of the respondents before us we have alloyed the learned Counsel appearing for both the parties to make their submission on the said question of non-joiner of parties as well. 

 22. The question as has been raised as to the defect of parties was argued for the first time in the Court of the First Appeal as has been notice above, and found favour with the learned Judges of the High Court Division. It appears that the plaintiffs put in certain documents being Exits 10 series for the purpose of showing that the plaintiffs exercised their right of possession in respect of the disputed lands by executing deeds of transfer in favour of certain persons subsequent to their acquisition of the right of tenancy by virtue of the disputed settlement. Such transferees, on the face of the said deeds of transfer, appear to have title and possession in the disputed lands and having regard to the frame of the suit they were certainly necessary parties in the suit, as the decree which may be passed in the suit is likely to affect their interest. It is true that the decoct of parties for the non-joiner of the transferees of Ext. 10 series has not been pleaded and in terms of Order 1, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure all objections on the ground of non-joiner or mis-joinder of parties ought to have been taken at the earliest possible opportunity and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived. Having regard to the law of procedure, it can pertinently be contended that the defendants cannot raise the question of non-joiner of parties for the first time in the Court of first appeal.
